analysis: All three are technically excellent and senior-appropriate, converging on a Redis dirty-flag / version-fence pattern with client-token versioning as the alternative, so calibration is uniformly high. The discriminator is style and proportionality against a user who prefers concise, opinionated answers. C wins: it leads with the answer, stays decisive, names exactly one real tradeoff, and is the shortest while still committing to a recommendation. B is a close second â€” focused and opinionated but padded with a full fallback design and a redundant recap section. A is last: it is the most verbose, opens with a meta preamble, restates the problem, and enumerates sub-options and a ship plan, matching the prompt's length instead of cutting through it â€” the exact behavior the user dislikes.
